items.t: JD.com Completes Takeover of MediaMarkt Owner Ceconomy; EU Terms Open Logistics to Rivals
sum: Chinese retailer JD.com completed its takeover of Ceconomy, the Düsseldorf-based parent of the MediaMarkt and Saturn electronics chains, on November 12, 2026. Under commitments the parties offered and the European Commission accepted, JD.com must now sell warehousing, logistics and technology services to rival retailers on the same terms it gives Ceconomy for 10 years.

The Commission granted conditional clearance on November 3 after concluding that Chinese subsidies to JD.com could distort competition inside the EU. JD.com refuted the subsidy allegations in May, saying the acquisition would not be financed by Chinese subsidies.

Published summaries of that clearance describe subsidy remedies and do not mention customer-data protections, according to Paul Weiss's summary. Data safeguards come instead from a separate Italian government decree and from JD.com's own pledges, and no independent audit of those safeguards appears in the reporting reviewed for this article.

Ceconomy runs more than 1,000 stores in 11 markets and employs more than 50,000 people, so the terms reach shoppers, workers and rival retailers that may want JD.com's logistics network. The sections below separate what the EU remedy covers, what it leaves to other rules and what remains unverified.
JD.com Holds 85.2% of Ceconomy With Convergenta After Cash Takeover

JD.com bought 59.8% of Ceconomy's share capital and voting rights through its indirect subsidiary Jingdong Holding Germany GmbH at €4.60 (approximately $5.12) per share in cash, for total consideration of €1.335 billion (approximately $1.49 billion).

Convergenta, an existing Ceconomy shareholder, keeps about 25.3%, which brings the combined holding to 85.2%. The July 30, 2025 offer valued Ceconomy at about €2.2 billion (approximately $2.45 billion), a premium of about 43% to its three-month average share price before talks became public.

Earnings Outlook Could Be A Key Test For JD.com Stock (JD)
sum: JD.com is back in focus after recent analyst commentary turned more cautious on near term earnings, even as forecasts still point to higher revenue and EPS ahead of the November 17, 2026 results release.

Sentiment is being pulled in opposite directions, as hedge fund manager Michael Burry calls JD.com deeply undervalued, while earnings estimate revisions and a Sell ranking from Zacks flag growing concern about execution and near term profit pressure.
We will now look at how JD.com's cautious earnings revisions, despite forecasts for growth, may reshape its broader investment narrative.

Compare JD.com's mixed sentiment with a curated set of other potential value ideas by scanning the 36 high quality undervalued stocks that have been picked for strong fundamentals and discounted pricing.

To own JD.com today, you need to believe the business can turn a broad e commerce and logistics footprint into healthier, more consistent profitability. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on margin improvement in JD Retail, logistics and newer services, while keeping heavy AI, robotics and overseas spending from diluting returns.

The biggest near term catalyst is the November 17 earnings release, where revenue trends and segment margins will signal how that balance is progressing. The main risk right now is execution on capital heavy projects in logistics and international hubs, which could hold back cash generation if returns stay muted.

The most relevant fresh datapoint is that analysts expect JD.com to report sharply higher EPS and higher revenue year over year on November 17, while the stock trades at a discount to peers and to some intrinsic value estimates. That sets expectations around operational progress and efficiency gains across retail and logistics.

The consumer discretionary sector faces an uneven global demand environment as consumers navigate persistent price pressures, changing spending priorities and uncertainty around economic growth.

Higher borrowing costs and cautious household spending have weighed on demand for big-ticket purchases, travel and other discretionary categories. At the same time, retailers and consumer brands are contending with changing shopping habits, promotional activity and pressure to maintain margins.

Global consumer spending trends also remain closely tied to developments in China and the U.S., two important markets for discretionary companies. China's retail sales growth, evolving domestic consumption patterns and the trajectory of U.S. household demand remain important indicators for companies across apparel, automobiles, luxury goods, restaurants and travel.

Hong Kong AI Stocks Retreat en Masse as Hang Seng Index Pares Gains; Turnover Hits Four-Week Low
sum: Hong Kong stocks opened higher but closed lower on November 9, with upward momentum clearly fading after a string of rebounds. The Hang Seng Index briefly climbed to 24,625 points in morning trade before swinging lower and closing down 0.13%. The China Enterprises Index fell 0.17%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 0.92%. Trading activity shrank in tandem, with full-day turnover of just HK$173.707 billion (approximately $22.2 billion), the lowest in about four weeks, signaling that investors are staying on the sidelines amid uncertainty over the outlook for AI trades.

Large internet stocks were the main drag on the market. Meituan (03690.HK) closed down 6.5%, while Xiaomi (01810.HK), JD.com (09618.HK), Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) and Alibaba (09988.HK) all reversed early gains to close lower. In morning trade, the Hang Seng Tech Index had opened up 1.02%, lifted by a 1.09% rebound in the Nasdaq and a more than 4% gain in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index on Friday. Alibaba opened up 2.19%, Tencent rose 1.29%, Xiaomi gained nearly 2%, and chip stocks including SMIC (00981.HK) and Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) also firmed in line with overseas markets. But the rebound failed to hold through the close.

Sector divergence persisted. AI hardware names continued to correct, with PCB and optical communications stocks—among the biggest gainers earlier—leading declines. Brokerages, shipping, autos and lithium battery shares also weakened, while the consumer sector, which had been active in recent sessions, pulled back. Money instead flowed into defensive assets, with coal, banks and other dividend-rich, high-yield sectors strengthening again to support the market. Biopharmaceutical stocks also put in a showing.

Short-selling data reflected growing caution. Total short-selling turnover in Hong Kong stocks reached HK$25.248 billion (approximately $3.2 billion), or 15% of total market turnover, with the short-selling ratio showing signs of climbing. Xiaomi-W, Tencent Holdings and Alibaba-W topped the short-selling list at HK$1.54 billion (approximately $196.4 million), HK$1.209 billion (approximately $154.2 million) and HK$1.09 billion (approximately $139.0 million), respectively.

JD.com Acquires MediaMarkt and Saturn: EU Approves Ceconomy Deal with Conditions
sum: JD.com’s acquisition of MediaMarkt and Saturn has been approved. On November 3, 2026, the European Commission gave the green light for the Chinese retail group to acquire Ceconomy, the parent company of MediaMarktSaturn, but only subject to conditions that will remain in effect for ten years. This cleared the final regulatory hurdle: According to Reuters, JD.com plans to close the deal by November 12. Europe’s largest electronics retailer will then be majority-owned by a Chinese conglomerate.
- The European Commission has approved JD.com’s acquisition of Ceconomy (MediaMarkt, Saturn, MediaWorld) under the Third-Country Subsidies Regulation.
- The Commission considers it proven that JD.com has received subsidies from China that could distort competition.
- JD.com must finance Ceconomy on market terms and offer its logistics and technology services to other retailers under the same conditions.
- The conditions will remain in effect for ten years and will be monitored by an independent trustee.
- JD.com is offering 4.60 euros per share and, together with the Kellerhals family, already holds 85.2 percent. The transaction is expected to close by November 12.

From an antitrust perspective, the deal was never the issue. The Federal Cartel Office had approved the takeover early on without any conditions because JD.com has played virtually no role in the electronics retail market in Germany to date. Brussels, however, asked itself a different question: Is a company here making a purchase with money provided by the Chinese government?

Michael Burry Sees This Fintech Stock Doubling or More
sum: Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) sees a possible buyout price of $100 to $120 per share for Fiserv (FISV), or 100% to 140% above its recent price of about $50.
He used reported private equity interest in Global Payments GPN as a yardstick, applying a similar multiple of about seven times profit to Fiserv. He also cited insider buying.

Burry said Fiserv has been held back by overly ambitious growth targets from prior management and poorly disclosed gains from Argentine hyperinflation. At about $50, he believes the stock could return 15% or more annually, and he plans to keep his position.

Burry also added to positions in BYD (BYDDY), Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM) and JD.com (JD), without disclosing the size of the purchases. The Sprouts additions are 2028 LEAP call options, long-dated contracts that give the right to buy shares at a set price, while JD's are 2029 calls.
He likened Hong Kong stocks' slide since the Hang Seng Index's 2021 peak to the Great Depression. He also reiterated a positive view on PayPal PYPL at prices in the $50s.

Alibaba, JD.com, PDD Stocks Climb Monday After Brutal October for Chinese Stocks: What’s Going On?
sum: Alibaba Group Holding Limited BABA, JD.com, Inc. JD and PDD Holdings Inc. PDD are trading higher Monday after a report that China’s central bank and securities regulator will meet to discuss tools designed to support the country’s capital market.
- Alibaba stock is trading at elevated levels. What should traders watch with BABA?
China Regulators, Central Bank to Meet on Stock Market Support Measures

According to Bloomberg, the People’s Bank of China will meet with the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the China Securities Regulatory Commission and major banks on Monday to study how to improve a relending program for share buybacks and stake increases. Bloomberg cited a report Sunday from Cailian, which cited people in the industry. Some securities firms and funds have received notices about the meeting, according to the 21st Century Business Herald, as cited by Bloomberg. The newspaper said industry participants speculated that the meeting was likely preparation by financial regulators for further action to stabilize the market.
The Meeting Follows China’s Worst Month for Stocks in More Than a Decade

Bloomberg said a state-backed effort would add to steps China took last month to stabilize its equity market. Those measures have so far proved insufficient, Bloomberg reported, against the backdrop of a weak domestic economy and doubts over AI earnings, with Chinese stocks suffering their worst month in more than a decade. The CSI 300 Index fell into a bear market in October, dropping 8.5% and falling for a record 12 straight weeks. Bloomberg also noted that China’s official manufacturing and non-manufacturing purchasing managers’ indexes fell back into contraction in October.

JD.com, Inc. (JD) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: JD.com, Inc. operates as a supply chain-based technology and service provider in the People's Republic of China and Europe. It operates through three segments: JD Retail, JD Logistics, and New Businesses. The company provides home appliances; mobile handsets and other digital products; computers, including desktop, laptop, and other various products, as well as printers and other office equipment; furniture and household goods; apparel; cosmetics and other personal care items; and pet products. It offers women's shoes, bags, watches, jewelry, and luxury goods; men's shoes, sports gear, and fitness equipment; automobiles and accessories; maternal and childcare products; toys and musical instruments; food, beverages, and fresh produce; gifts, flowers, and plants; and pharmaceutical and healthcare products, such as OCT pharmaceutical products, nutritional supplements, healthcare services, and other healthcare equipment. In addition, the company provides books, e-books, music, movies, and other media products; virtual goods consisting of online travel agency, attraction tickets, and prepaid phone cards and game cards; industrial products; and installation and maintenance services. Further, it offers online marketplace services for third-party merchants; marketing services; and omni-channel solutions to customers and offline retailers, as well as online healthcare services. Additionally, the company develops, owns, and manages its logistics facilities and other real estate properties to support third parties; and offers asset management services and integrated service platform; leasing of storage facilities and related management services, as well as engages in online retail business; technology-driven supply chain solutions; and logistics services. The company was formerly known as 360buy Jingdong Inc. and changed its name to JD.com, Inc. in January 2014. JD.com, Inc. was incorporated in 2006 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

sum: China's biggest artificial intelligence spender is leading a sharp retreat in U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks even as American large caps push higher, raising questions about whether heavy cloud spending is becoming a liability rather than an advantage.

Selling in U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks is landing hardest on the group’s biggest artificial intelligence spender, even as American large caps edge higher. Alibaba Group (NYSE:BABA | BABA Price Prediction) shares are down 5% to $103.67 in morning trading, a slide that puts the e-commerce and cloud giant at the front of the China tech retreat.

Meanwhile, JD.com (NASDAQ:JD) stock is down 4% to $25.65, a decline that trails the drop in Alibaba stock by a narrow margin. PDD Holdings (NASDAQ:PDD) shares are down 4% to $78.21, a move that lands in step with JD.com. That tight cluster among Alibaba, JD.com and PDD shares stands out while American buyers are otherwise buying into equities.

Among funds, the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (NYSEARCA:KWEB) is down 3% to $23.53. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.5% to $772.84. Thus, U.S. large-caps are holding up better than the KWEB ETF, BABA stock, JD stock, and PDD stock today.

Alibaba, JD.com and PDD shares are falling by similar amounts alongside the China internet fund while the S&P 500 tracker is higher. That pattern shows the selling spread across U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks as a group, with the pressure landing on marketplace, direct retail and discount commerce models alike.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is the chip supplier at the center of a Reuters report published in the prior session. Citing two people familiar with the matter, Reuters said ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent had placed large orders. The focus was an NVIDIA workstation chip that can still be sold to Chinese buyers under U.S. export limits. The news service also reported that NVIDIA may be able to fill only a small share of those orders. That leaves open whether the story bears on Alibaba’s heavy artificial intelligence spending.

sum: JD.com (ISIN US47215P1066) is being reassessed after Barclays cut its price target from USD 41.00 to USD 38.00 while maintaining an Overweight rating. Markets Insider reported the change on October 14, 2026. JD.com stock was at EUR 23.75 at Lang & Schwarz on October 20, 2026 at 8:30 p.m. CEST.

Barclays expects third-quarter revenue to be broadly in line, while rising expenses could offset gross-margin improvement, according to the report. The lower target followed a reduction in the valuation multiple from 6 times expected fiscal year 2027 EBITDA to 5 times, while the firm retained its Overweight rating.

JD.com reported total revenue of RMB 346.00 billion for the second quarter of 2026, down 2.90 percent from the prior-year quarter. Non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders rose 20.80 percent year over year to RMB 8.90 billion, and non-GAAP net margin increased 0.50 percentage points to 2.60 percent, according to the Yahoo Finance transcript published August 13, 2026.

JD.com was trading at USD 26.70 on the Nasdaq on October 20, 2026 at 2:31 p.m. ET. Its market capitalization was USD 36.10 billion, and its trailing price-to-earnings ratio was 17.38. The 52-week Nasdaq range was USD 24.51 to USD 35.06.

items.t: Alibaba Surges 9% Ahead of Earnings, Baidu Gains 5% as Chinese E-Commerce and Tech Stocks Rally
sum: Shares of Alibaba (NYSE:BABA | BABA Price Prediction) are up 9% to $106 and change in early Wednesday trading, leading a broad rally in Chinese internet and e-commerce names. Alibaba stock closed at $98.14 on Tuesday, and even after this…

The move extends well beyond Alibaba. Baidu (NASDAQ:BIDU) shares are up 5% to $117.99, JD.com (NASDAQ:JD) shares are up 3% to $27.40, and PDD Holdings (NASDAQ:PDD) shares are up 2% to $84. Alibaba’s Hong Kong-listed shares climbed as much as 12%, the biggest jump since September.

Traders are rotating into beaten-down Chinese mega-caps after a sharp selloff in South Korea and Taiwan chipmakers, with the Kospi falling 5%. That regional shuffle is doing a lot of the work today, layered on top of a stock-specific catalyst at Alibaba.

The specific spark came from a pre-earnings analyst briefing indicating that losses in Alibaba’s highly competitive instant-commerce business narrowed last quarter, while overall profitability held steady. The report was first surfaced by local outlet Jiemian, and it landed in a market already primed for good news out of China.

That matters because instant commerce has been the biggest drag on Alibaba’s margins. The company’s fiscal Q4 2026 report on May 13 showed adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization (EBITA) dropping 84% to $740 million on a $123 million operating loss, even as revenue grew to $35.3 billion. Any signal that the losses are slowing down changes the setup into the next earnings report.

The AI and cloud story remains the other pillar of the bull case for Alibaba. The company’s Cloud Intelligence Group revenue grew 38% last quarter, and AI-related product revenue reached 30% of external cloud revenue for the 11th consecutive quarter of triple-digit AI growth. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu has been emphatic about full-stack AI investment as the strategic priority.

Baidu, JD.com, and PDD Holdings are moving in sympathy rather than on company-specific news. The rotation trade is being driven by valuation; all three of these stocks are in the red on a year-to-date basis in 2026, leaving them well below where the group started the year.

Can Alibaba's Digital Commerce Ecosystem Drive FY2027 Growth?
sum: Alibaba's BABA digital commerce strategy is evolving into a more integrated, AI-enabled retail ecosystem that could support growth in fiscal 2027. Rather than relying solely on gross merchandise volume expansion, Alibaba is enhancing merchant productivity, consumer engagement and platform monetization across Taobao, Tmall and its instant commerce offerings. The company has also revamped its merchant development program by linking platform subsidies to merchants' marketing spend, an initiative aimed at improving advertising penetration and long-term monetization. These efforts are already gaining traction, with customer management revenue (CMR) increasing 8% year over year on a like-for-like basis in the March quarter, while China E-commerce Group revenues rose 6% to RMB 122 billion.

Quick commerce has become a strategic extension of Alibaba's broader retail platform rather than a standalone business. Order volume expanded 2.7 times year over year, supporting stronger growth at Freshippo and Tmall Supermarket while helping drive double-digit monthly active consumer additions for the Taobao app. At the same time, the integration of the Qwen app with Taobao, Tmall, Alipay, Amap and Fliggy is embedding AI-driven search, discovery and shopping assistance across Alibaba's consumer ecosystem, creating additional opportunities to improve user engagement and purchase frequency over time.

These investments have weighed on near-term profitability, with Alibaba China E-commerce Group's adjusted EBITA declining 40% year over year as spending on quick commerce, technology and user experience increased. However, improving fulfillment efficiency, higher average order values and stronger unit economics indicate that these investments are becoming more productive. If Alibaba continues translating higher consumer engagement into stronger merchant spending while improving the profitability of its quick commerce operations, its integrated digital commerce ecosystem could emerge as a meaningful catalyst for fiscal 2027 growth.
Alibaba faces intense competition from PDD Holdings PDD and JD.com JD, both of which continue to invest in strengthening their digital commerce ecosystems.

When All Things Considered– Sales of Durian Increased 17x in the First Hour of JD 618
sum: On June 1st, the first day of JD’s 618 Grand Promotion, transaction volume of fresh food increased over 8 times year-on-year. Among the many best-selling products is durian, a seasonal fruit that is increasingly welcomed by Chinese consumers. In the first hour of 618, transaction volume of durian on JD increased over 17 times compared with the same period last year.

In Asia, durian is known as the “king of fruits.” As early as in April this year, JD imported multiple durian varieties from Thailand including the popular Golden Pillow, rare Puangmanee and Chanee. The total volume filled thirty 40ft containers.
Every durian imported by JD goes through a comprehensive screening process. In the early stages of picking, JD.com’s fresh food business team will cooperate with growers directly to ensure quality.

“During the epidemic, we specifically worked on a stricter quality control plan. To put it simply, every durian from Thailand needs to go through at least six testing procedures and meet over 10 specifications before it can be delivered to our customers,” said Wen Li from JD Fresh’s quality control team.

JD will typically pick the durian to be exported to China when it is about 75% ripe, so that the durian is tastiest 7 days later when it arrives. Once at JD’s warehouse in China, the fruit will need to pass several evaluations, ensuring, for example, that the fruit cracks at the standard diameter, ripeness, weight, shape and sweetness meet the standard, and more. Durian that does not pass the evaluation screening will not go for sale on JD. Even after being accepted to JD’s warehouse, JD’s quality control team will do regular checks to make sure every durian sold to its customers is of high quality.
Durians are most popular in first and second-tier Chinese cities like Beijing and Guangzhou, but demand is growing in lower-tier regions where previously the fruit was not easily accessible.

As China’s largest fresh food retail platform, JD now offers 320,000 SKUs (stock-keeping-units) covering seafood, fruit, vegetables, meat and poultry and more from over 50 countries and regions. JD offers various fresh food, including durians from Thailand and Malaysia, through its online channel JD Fresh and offline supermarket chain 7FRESH.

JD.com Q1 2026 earnings preview: food delivery losses in focus
sum: JD.com reports Q1 2026 results on 12 May, with analysts forecasting a revenue re-acceleration to 3.2% YoY and EBITDA margin recovery as food delivery losses begin to ease.

JD.com closed the fourth quarter (Q4) 2025 with group revenue up 1.5% year-on-year (YoY) to RMB352.3 billion. JD Retail, the group's core operating segment, posted a 2% YoY revenue decline. Electronics and home appliances contracted 12% against a demanding comparison base from the 2024 government trade-in subsidy programme, with the shortfall only partially offset by 12% general merchandise growth. Nevertheless, JD Retail's full-year operating margin expanded for the sixth consecutive year, reaching 4.6%.

Profitability at the group level, however, came under significant pressure from continued investment in the food delivery segment. Full-year net income attributable to ordinary shareholders fell sharply to RMB19.6 billion from RMB41.4 billion in 2024, while free cash flow contracted to RMB6 billion from RMB44 billion.
The standout positive was user momentum: annual active customers surpassed 700 million, with shopping frequency rising over 40% YoY, underscoring the growing engagement of JD's retail ecosystem.
Analysts expect JD.com's revenue growth to re-accelerate to 3.2% YoY in Q1 2026, recovering from the trough recorded last quarter.

Net income attributable to shareholders is projected to return to positive territory after the net loss of RMB2.7 billion in Q4 2025. On a YoY basis, however, net income is forecast to decline 58.4%, reflecting the continued drag from elevated marketing expenditure - particularly within the food delivery business.

Non-GAAP earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) margin is expected to recover from its recent trough to the highest level since Q1 2025, consistent with management's prior guidance that food delivery investment has peaked.

Burry wrote in a late April post that GameStop, JD.com, and Molina Healthcare were his three largest positions, and together made up well over a third of his personal stock portfolio.
